newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BUND VOL SLIPS, PUT SPREADS DOMINATE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BUND VOL SLIPS, PUT SPREADS DOMINATE.

text.p: Implied volatility of LIFFE Bund options dropped on Friday in firm put volume, but has scope to turn back upwards again next week, options dealers said.
"Volatility has been coming down, but this Bundesbank repo story is not going away, and we have important numbers from the U.S. next week," said one options salesman from a European bank.
"You should be buying volatility on dips."

At-the-money September options exercisable into the September Bund future were quoted at 5.31 percent, down from 5.45-5.60 percent at the open. The September Bund future was trading at 101.64 at 1215 GMT, down 38 basis points.
The Bundesbank will set its next repo tender on Tuesday, amid speculation it will switch to a variable rate repo and allow money market interest rates to rise.
In the U.S., retail sales, producer price, consumer price and industrial production data for July will be released next week.
Bund volatility will fall further on Friday ahead of the weekend, before swinging back up next week, options dealers said.
"It's going to be quiet for the rest of the day," said one LIFFE broker from a U.S. firm.

Activity was brisk in September put options, dealers said. One broker sold the one-by-two 101.00/102.00 put spread. The trade involves selling the 102.00 strike and buying the 101.00 strike in double quantities.
Around 1,000 contracts went through in the transaction, dealers said. Other put spreads also traded, in both Bunds and BTPs, they added.
By 1215 GMT, 4,935 contracts had traded in the September 101.00 Bund put, 4,830 contracts in the 101.50 put and 4,425 lots in the 102.00 put.
In BTPs, 2,475 contracts traded in the September 134.00 put and 2,330 lots in the 135.00 put.
